target_customer: Cancer patients and, in the long run, healthy adults, reached through pharma partners, regulators and hospitals (a drug developer, not a software seller)
problem: Oncogenes such as KRAS are poorly recognized by the immune system, so they are hard to target with vaccines. Adventris builds an off-the-shelf vaccine aimed at the most common KRAS mutations.
business_model: Biotech drug development, funded by venture capital and later by partnerships or licensing; first product is a pre-clinical KRAS peptide vaccine

technical_complexity.rationale: A pan-KRAS off-the-shelf cancer vaccine needs preclinical immunology, GMP manufacturing and multi-year clinical trials; for a seven-person team this is research-grade and regulatory-gated.

defensibility.rationale: Technology is licensed from Johns Hopkins according to a secondary profile (terms not public), and clinical data and trial approvals would form a moat, but KRAS vaccines were also pursued by other groups and the lead asset is pre-clinical.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy reported by sources found; other KRAS vaccine programs run in parallel (Elicio's ELI-002 has published phase 1 data in 2025).

market_need_then: KRAS is the most common cancer oncogene and has long been considered hard to target; immunotherapy and neoantigen vaccine research was active at Johns Hopkins and elsewhere, giving a clear scientific rationale for the company in 2022 to 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses adventris.com (exact name .com as of the YC listing).

identity.visual_style: unclear; company site is a minimal single page

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found; a search for the name only returned similarly named unrelated firms, though in biotech the brand matters little at this stage.

outcome_analysis: Adventris is an active, early biotech with a pre-clinical KRAS vaccine and a founding team that pairs a Johns Hopkins oncologist with biotech commercial leaders. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Profiles say first human dosing is targeted around 2027, so the outcome is still open and funding adequacy cannot be judged from public data.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators disagree (a $12.5M seed dated Oct 2024 on Caplight and Standout, a $12M seed in a JHU Startups PDF snippet, about $500K pre-seed or convertible note on CB Insights and VCBacked, $125K on Extruct). No press release or filing was found, so no round is recorded. The Caplight page banner about a $16M Series A appears unrelated. Reported investors on aggregators: Y Combinator, Refactor Capital, Blackbird BioVentures, Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures. The YC launch described lung cancer as the first target while later profiles say pancreatic cancer. Johns Hopkins license is from a secondary profile only. Competition list left empty because no sources dated near early 2023 were found. Liz Jaffee added from the YC launch post.
